items.es: futuro continuo: will be + verbo-ing (lo que estará pasando en un momento del futuro)

example.en: Don't call me at eight tomorrow. I'll be driving.
example.es: No me llames mañana a las ocho. Voy a estar manejando.

example.en: This time tomorrow, I'll be flying to Rome.
example.es: Mañana a esta hora voy a estar volando a Roma.

items.es: futuro perfecto: will have + participio (lo que ya habrá pasado)

example.en: By the end of the year, we'll have saved enough money.
example.es: Para fin de año, habremos ahorrado suficiente dinero.

items.es: para, a más tardar (by Friday = para el viernes)

example.en: Please send me the report by Friday.
example.es: Por favor, mándame el informe para el viernes.

items.term: Will you be + -ing? (polite questions about plans)
items.es: pregunta amable sobre los planes de alguien

example.en: Will you be using the car tonight?
example.es: ¿Vas a usar el auto esta noche?

items.term: future perfect continuous (I'll have been working)
items.es: futuro perfecto continuo: cuánto tiempo llevarás haciendo algo

example.en: By June, she'll have been working here for ten years.
example.es: En junio va a cumplir diez años trabajando aquí.

passages.title: A busy month ahead
passages.text: Next month will be busy for the team. On the first Monday, we'll be moving to the new office, so please don't plan any meetings that day. By Wednesday, the technicians will have installed the new computers. Laura will be traveling for most of the month, so she won't be answering emails every day. By the end of the month, we'll have finished the first part of the project, and in December I'll have been working with this team for five years.

options: At nine tomorrow I'll working.
At nine tomorrow I'll be working.
At nine tomorrow I'm be working.

exercises.sentence: This time tomorrow, I'll be flying to Rome.
options: Ayer a esta hora estaba volando a Roma.
